hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, for example astrocytes, APOE4 causes impaired ARF6-related recycling of receptors between the cell surface and the endosome, compared with APOE3.
A: APOE genotype or apoE isoform (APOE4 vs APOE3)
B: ARF6-related recycling of receptors between the cell surface and the endosome (e.g. ABCA1, LRP1, receptor surface levels, recycling rate)
scope: IN: recycling of receptors between cell surface and endosomes (surface levels of receptors such as ABCA1, LRP1, LDLR, ApoER2, glutamate receptors; internalization and recycling rates; Rab11/Rab4 recycling-compartment localization; receptor retention in late endosomes), and ARF6 abundance/activity and its manipulation, in an APOE4 vs APOE3 context or a rescue in APOE4 cells. OUT: receptor transcription without trafficking readouts, downstream functions (cholesterol efflux, amyloid clearance) unless used as the only surrogate of recycling, unrelated signalling.

row.Finding quote: Brain tissue fractionation showed a significant decrease in total membrane caveolin-1 levels in HPCD treated-APOE4-TR mice, along with enhanced ABCA1 recycling, as indicated by increased membrane ABCA1 levels (Fig. 5 F).
row.Finding summary: (PBS -> HPCD in APOE4-TR mice) -> (increased cortical membrane-enriched ABCA1 and decreased caveolin-1)

row.Finding description: HPTLC analysis of secreted cholesterol, cholesteryl esters (CE), and phosphatidylethanolamine (PE) in APOE-isogenic human iAstrocytes showed significantly lower cholesterol and CE secretion in APOE4 than APOE3, providing an indirect ABCA1-function surrogate.
row.Finding quote: Interestingly, secreted cholesterol and CE were significantly decreased only in APOE4 iAstrocytes (Figures S2A and S2B).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower cholesterol and CE secretion in human iAstrocytes)
row.Experimental system: Human quiescent iPSC-derived astrocytes from EBiSC CRISPR-generated APOE-isogenic lines BIONi010-C-2 (APOE3) and BIONi010-C-4 (APOE4), each expressing a single APOE allele; differentiated through neural progenitor cells using a 44-day astrocyte differentiation protocol; baseline without cytokine stimulation; secreted lipids measured by HPTLC and normalized to cellular phosphatidylcholine.

proposed.why: Was 3/4. Cholesterol and CE secretion depends also on apoE4 lipidation and cholesterol synthesis; it is a downstream function with several routes besides receptor recycling, a weakly coupled surrogate: class 3, strength 5, the same for all three P14 functional readouts.

row.Finding description: Across three independent experiments, flow cytometry showed a lower baseline Aβ42 uptake trend in APOE4 versus APOE3 human isogenic iAstrocytes with no significant difference (p = 0.054), while RAP significantly decreased uptake in APOE3 but caused no significant difference in APOE4 (p = 0.23).
row.Finding quote: A flow-cytometry-based Aβ42 uptake assay, using pre-aggregated Hilyte488-tagged Aβ42, showed an allele-dependent trend in uptake capacity (KO > E2 > E3 ≥ E4), although differences between APOE3 and APOE4 did not reach significance (p = 0.054) (Figure 2F). Interestingly, APOE-KO cells showed the highest Aβ42 uptake capacity. Aβ42 is mostly taken up through receptor-dependent endocytosis, such as LRP1. To determine if Aβ uptake in iAstrocytes is mediated by LDLR-dependent endocytosis, we treated cells with a low concentration of LDLR family antagonist receptor-associated protein (RAP), which primarily blocked LRP1 and very-low-density lipoprotein receptor (VLDLR), in order to induce a mild reduction in Aβ uptake, resulting in a measurable difference between genotypes. Blocking LDLR family members caused a significant decrease in Aβ uptake in APOE-KO, E2, and E3, but not in E4 iAstrocytes (p = 0.23).
row.Finding summary: Baseline uptake trended lower in APOE4 than APOE3 (p = 0.054). RAP significantly reduced uptake in APOE3. Its effect in APOE4 did not reach significance (p = 0.23). The paper gives no genotype-by-RAP interaction test.
row.Experimental system: Human APOE-isogenic iAstrocytes assayed by flow cytometry for the percentage of live Aβ-positive cells using 1 μM pre-aggregated labeled Aβ42, with or without 24 h pretreatment with 0.2 μM RAP. The supplied text does not verify two-hour Aβ exposure or continued RAP during exposure.

proposed.why: Was 3/4. Abeta42 uptake runs through several receptors and phagocytosis; it is a downstream function with several routes besides receptor recycling, a weakly coupled surrogate: class 3, strength 5, the same for all three P14 functional readouts.

row.Finding description: Across three independent experiments comparing glutamate uptake over 1 hour in APOE-isogenic human iAstrocytes, APOE4 cells showed lower uptake than APOE3 and the lowest uptake overall, providing an indirect functional surrogate for transporter availability without measuring ARF6-related recycling.
row.Finding quote: Uptake of glutamate in iAstrocytes demonstrated an allele-dependent effect, with APOE4 iAstrocytes taking up the lowest amount of glutamate while APOE2 and APOE-KO took up the highest amounts (Figure 2D).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower glutamate uptake in human iAstrocytes)
row.Experimental system: Human monoallelic EBiSC APOE3 and APOE4 iAstrocytes differentiated through day 44 and plated 24 h before assay. Glutamate uptake over 1 h was normalized to total lysate protein. The supplied text does not specify glutamine deprivation, glutamate concentration, assay temperature, or detection reagent.

proposed.why: Was 3/4. Glutamate uptake depends on transporter expression and energy state; it is a downstream function with several routes besides receptor recycling, a weakly coupled surrogate: class 3, strength 5, the same for all three P14 functional readouts.
